A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BioTUCH work. All ten pages of each were readable and compared, including equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original contact-detection measurements, pose-reconstruction comparisons and loss ablations in Section 5 and Table 2, and two in-the-wild demonstrations.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original empirical results, including contact-detection sensitivity and specificity, quantitative pose comparisons, ablations, and in-the-wild demonstrations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the identical bioimpedance contact detector and SMPL-X arm-pose optimization, including arm selection, masked updates, losses, stopping conditions, and temporal smoothing.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three-participant dataset with 82 self-touch gestures and nine adversarial non-contact gestures, plus the same two in-the-wild sequences.

E2.justification: Section 5.2 and Table 2 retain Multi-HMR, AiOS, and TUCH, with the same BioTUCH extensions and loss variants. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The protocols are identical: 57 manually labeled gestures for detection evaluation and per-frame pose evaluation before smoothing, using the same ground truth, Procrustes alignment, and reconstruction/contact metrics.

E4.justification: The loss ablations in Table 2, robustness analysis across input reconstruction errors in Figure 5, and qualitative and failure cases in Figures 6–8 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical. Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the fitted-curve reporting in Figure 5 is also unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match. For example, both report sensitivity 0.858 and specificity 0.992, while Table 2 gives Multi-HMR PA-V2V of 57.46 mm without BioTUCH and 50.21 mm with it.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and optimization equations (1)–(4) are identical. No assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusions retain the same contributions and scope, including the claimed average 11.7% reconstruction improvement, contact-aware dataset, and miniature wearable sensor.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations are identical, including contact-loss dominance, dependence on initial mesh accuracy, difficulties with simultaneous contacts, and premature stopping caused by finger-articulation errors.

D1.justification: Sensor hardware, sampling parameters, processing thresholds, capture and synchronization details, and optimization documentation are unchanged. The stated code/data availability and project link are also identical.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 25 references are unchanged, as are the novelty claims and positioning relative to visual self-contact estimation and sensor-based contact detection.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 4 December 2025 to v2 dated 12 March 2026. The title, authors, prose, terminology, and section structure are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8, Tables 1–2, captions, and page layout are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–10 are pixel-identical; page 1 differs only in the arXiv margin stamp.

improvement.justification: The only visible revision is the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific content, empirical evidence, limitations, reproducibility information, and substantive presentation are identical, establishing no meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
